comments.author: @DistantStraits
comments.text: A large share of national income comes from selling tuna fishing licences to foreign fleets working in their waters. A country most people can't place on a map is a significant player in one of the world's biggest fisheries. That's the economy, not coconuts. Change my mind.

comments.author: @TheUnlistedWorld
comments.text: Kiribati spans more ocean than India spans land. Thirty three islands scattered across an area the size of a continent, and it's the only country sitting in all four hemispheres. Small is the wrong word entirely. It's a country made mostly of sea. Change my mind.

comments.author: @DiscoverGlobePlacesTop10_NL158
comments.text: More than 100,000 people live on islands only a few meters above the sea. would you stay and fight for your homeland- or leave before the ocenan forces you to ?

comments.author: @uncensoredworldtravel
comments.text: It is sobering to realize that a country doesn't have to sink to become uninhabitable; the loss of fresh water alone changes everything. This documentary puts the climate crisis into a raw, human perspective.

comments.author: @BulockHyun
comments.text: 이런 좋은 콘텐츠를 만들어 주셔서 감사합니다. 많이 배우고 갑니다.

comments.author: @fabulouslife-mm
comments.text: It’s heartbreaking to see how climate change and rising sea levels threaten their drinking water and homes. I truly hope the world pays more attention to Kiribati.

comments.author: @UntoldEarthDocs_Us
comments.text: People often talk about Kiribati “disappearing,” but the scarier point in this documentary is different: the islands don’t have to disappear for life to become unsustainable. What happens when your country still exists on the map, but everyday life there becomes almost impossible?

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: Living between the ocean and lagoon sounds like paradise... untill you realize that the same ocean can make your drinking wataer salty. Paradise or survival?

comments.author: @PlanetUncoveredOfficial
comments.text: It’s incredible how the people of Kiribati have adapted to life on such tiny islands for generations. The fact that they still want to protect their homeland instead of simply leaving really stayed with me. Beautiful documentary. 🌊❤
